To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of steel fiber and partial replacement of fly ash in concrete can improve the Impact resistance considerably.
the use of steel fiber reinforced concrete with flyash is an effective and economical way of increasing the Impact strength of concrete.

the Impact resistance of the concrete is enhanced by the inclusion of steel fibers in concrete, the Impact strength of flyash concrete is increased by the inclusion of flyash and the impact strength of the concrete can be increased further by the inclusion of both flyash and steel fibers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of high impact resistance concrete.
the impact behaviour of flyash reinforced concrete and fly ash fiber reinforced concrete.
the development of new concrete composite materials with high strength and high toughness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of fly ash and steel fibers in concrete would result in a significant improvement in the Impact resistance and durability of the concrete.
the Impact resistance of flyash concrete is improved by the addition of steel fibers.
the impact resistance of flyash concrete is improved with steel fiber addition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of steel fibers in the range of 0.5% and 1% by weight of the cement in flyash concrete would result in an improvement of 23% to 52% in Impact strength of the concrete composites.
the impact resistance of the flyash reinforced concrete with steel fiber was found to be higher than that of the conventional concrete.
the use of steel fibers in concrete is found to be very beneficial in enhancing the impact strength of the concrete.
The main takeaway from our work is that
steel fibers can be used to enhance the impact resistance of flyash concrete.
the Impact strength of the flyash concretes can be increased by using steel fibers in different proportions.
the use of fly ash as a partial replacement of cement is found to increase the strength of concrete, which is also confirmed from our work.
